newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to April 4.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to April 4.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 16.61 percent decline in its turnover in the week to April 4 as some commercial borrowers pulled out of the market and searched for fresh funds elsewhere.
Total turnover fell to 49.54 million dinars ($8.97 million) from 59.404 million dinars a week ago. The number of deals remained unchanged at 206.
One trader said commercial borrowers which had issued bourse-listed commercial paper were now increasingly discharging their liabilities and resorting to direct borrowing from banks.
Analysts said more direct bank commercial lending to companies did not result from a dramatically improved liquidity of the banking sector nor the lower price of their lending.
"Companies turn to banks purely on inertia. Besides, many companies are direct debtors to banks and must play by the banks' rules," said an analyst who asked not to be named.
For the week ending April 4, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 183 times for a volume of 30.785 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for six deals totalling 1.461 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 520 percent, while maturity stood between 10 and 30 days.
* The BSE reported one transaction in the central bank short-term bonds worth 0.3 million dinars.
Last week, the National Bank of Yugoslavia also put part of its bond portfolio on sale to compensate for funds previously given to Serbia's Commodity Reserve Agency to finance grain stockpiling.
Out of 88.8 million dinars offered, investors bought only 8.811 million dinars worth.
* There were three deals in wheat contracts totalling 4.582 million dinars.
The BSE said some secondary trading in wheat contracts appeared on Friday as one of the contract holders sold paper from its portfolio.
* The bourse reported two deals in certificates of deposit worth 0.6 million dinars.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper and treasury bills rose to 30.884 million dinars from 25.788 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, fell to 14.95 million dinars from 20 million a week ago. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
